android_mechanism: Progress broadcast emitted on every update; fix emits only when the value actually changes
bug_description: AVPlayerUtils' timeUpdate callback writes the millisecond-precision playback position into the global PLAY_TIME AppStorage state on every callback (about 10 times per second). The full player page binds PLAY_TIME via @StorageProp, so the heavy player view (cover art, controls, lyrics entry) re-renders at callback frequency even though the displayed progress only changes once per second, wasting UI-thread CPU during playback and draining battery.
fix_summary: The global state is written only when the whole-second part of the position changes (seek still updates immediately).
trigger_steps: Start playing any song and open the full player page; keep the screen on.
Start hitrace capture (categories: ace, app, sched, graphic).
Let the song play untouched for 60 seconds.
Stop hitrace. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: Count of player-page state-update/render passes attributable to PLAY_TIME changes during 60s of idle playback (ace trace component update events or JS state-set calls), plus UI-thread CPU time.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed ~600 state writes/minute (10/s); fixed ~60/minute (1/s). unfixed UI CPU time > fixed by a clearly measurable margin during playback.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 70 ace app sched graphic -o /data/local/tmp/cm_playtime.chtrace
